_comment: ADR 0052 §D2/§D7 — machine-readable release manifest and the single source of truth for REQUIRED UPGRADE STOPS. /cut-app-release PREPENDS each immutable vX.Y.Z release into `releases` (newest first) and sets `latest`. An upgrade tool reads `releases` to compute which required stops sit between a customer's current version and the target. `latest` names the newest stable (the moving alias the /install/ download points at). `requiredStop` (land on this version before going past it) and `rollingSafe` (the previous binary may keep running against this version's schema; false ⇒ stop every old instance first, even when skipping past it) are separate constraints (ADR 0052 §D2a); `node scripts/upgrade-plan.mjs <from> [<to>]` computes the plan. The per-entry field shape is documented in `_releaseShape` — that is a SCHEMA EXAMPLE, never a real release; do not parse it as one.

breakingConfig: The auth posture requires OPENWOP_AUTHORIZATION_ENFORCEMENT=true or OPENWOP_ALLOW_UNENFORCED_AUTHORIZATION=true (ADR 0981 P3).
When superadmins are configured in the auth posture, set OPENWOP_SUPERADMIN_REQUIRE_MFA=true or OPENWOP_ALLOW_SUPERADMIN_WITHOUT_MFA=true (ADR 0981 P3).
Postmark marketing/unlabelled sends require a Broadcast stream: default broadcast, or OPENWOP_POSTMARK_BROADCAST_STREAM naming an existing Broadcast stream (ADR 0994).
Production in-process WASI requires OPENWOP_CODE_EXEC_RUNTIME=wasi; a bundled runtime no longer enables it automatically (ADR 0995).

Workflow vector/search/NoSQL/blob names now resolve under wf:. Inventory and back up existing workflow data before upgrading; quiesce affected workflows and arrange a reviewed data transition. No automatic migration; never copy host-private data into the run namespace (ADR 0998).

Existing OpenSearch indexes use new physical names and need an operator-reviewed rebuild from authoritative tenant-scoped data; old colliding indexes must not be copied wholesale into one tenant. Back up, quiesce affected writers and verify isolation/counts/queries before resuming. No automatic data migration; coordinate the wf: transition where applicable (#5355).
OPENWOP_PROPOSALS_ACTIVATION removed (ADR 0938 D2); it had no working effect
OpenWOP v1 removed: /v1/* answers 410 (public read twins 308), discovery advertises only 2.0; OPENWOP_V1_RETIRED no longer exists (ADR 0812)
Chain packs must pin every node reference exactly (typeId@x.y.z) or they are refused at load (ADR 0766)
Registry packs must be signed for the v2 tree (ed25519-canonical-json) with engines admitting <3.0.0
OPENWOP_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS (new) — set it when a public-address proxy other than Google's front end fronts the backend (ADR 0851)
Scale-out hosts withhold memory-backed storage families; select OPENWOP_SURFACE_* shared backends (ADR 0867)

releases.rollingUnsafeReason: Postgres migration 37 / SQLite 39 rename invocation_log.provider_key to invocation_id; a 0.1.0 process sharing the upgraded database fails on that table. Recorded 2026-10-24 (ADR 0052 §D2a): the 0.2.0 release notes said this, but the manifest had no field for it.
breakingConfig: Webhook: pre-spec `openwop-signature: t=…,v1=…` and `openwop-subscription-id` headers removed — verify with the OpenWOP-* / X-openwop-* family
OPENWOP_RATELIMIT_IP_REQS_PER_MIN is now the WRITE budget; reads use OPENWOP_RATELIMIT_IP_READ_REQS_PER_MIN (ADR 0640)
OPENWOP_INTERRUPT_TOKEN_SECRET (new) — set it; the fallback is not a secret
Not rolling-safe: stop the 0.1.0 binary before starting 0.2.0 (invocation_log column rename)
